job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were helping their grandfather in the garden. Meera poured water into a glass jar filled with dry soil. As the water seeped in, tiny bubbles rose to the surface. 'Grandfather, why are those bubbles coming out?' she asked. Grandfather smiled and explained, 'The soil is not a solid block; it has tiny spaces filled with air. When water enters, it pushes that air out.' Later, they sat under a large tree. Meera wondered if the tree was breathing. Grandfather explained that plants take in carbon dioxide to make food, but they also respire like animals, using oxygen to release energy. He pointed to a fish tank nearby, noting that fish breathe the dissolved oxygen trapped in the water, not the oxygen atoms inside the water molecules themselves. As the sun set, they watched the sky. Grandfather mentioned that the atmosphere is a thin, protective blanket of gases surrounding Earth, not an endless layer reaching into space. He added that while we need oxygen to survive, nitrogen actually makes up most of the air, not oxygen. Finally, he showed them a cold glass of lemonade, explaining that the water droplets on the outside come from water vapour already present in the air, which turns into liquid when it touches the cold surface.
response.summary: The passage explains that air occupies space in soil and exists as a thin layer around Earth. It also clarifies that plants respire, fish use dissolved oxygen, and water vapour is always present in the air.
